findings.title: No re-check of cache after taking write lock (thundering herd)
findings.body: After the RLock check misses, every concurrent caller takes the write lock and then reloads the manifest from disk. The cache is not re-checked under the write lock. On a cold start, N concurrent requests will each read and parse assets-manifest.json serially. Re-check `entryPointAssetsCache != nil && cfg.Env != setting.Dev` after `Lock()` to avoid the duplicate work.

findings.title: Cache overwritten with nil result on error
findings.body: `entryPointAssetsCache = result` runs even when `err != nil`, in which case result is nil. A transient read failure therefore wipes a previously valid cache, which matters in Dev mode, where the code reloads on every call. Callers also receive a nil assets pointer alongside the error. The cache should only be assigned when err == nil.
